question: The simple interest and compound interest compounded annually on a certain sum of money with a given rate for a period of 2 years are Rs 700 and Rs 756 respectively the sum of money
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** for 2 years = 756 − 700 = ₹56.

**Simple Interest** for 1 year = 700 ÷ 2 = ₹350.

Rate of Interest (R) = (Difference ÷ SI for 1 year) × 100 = (56 ÷ 350) × 100 = 16%.

Sum of Money (P) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ R = (350 × 100) ÷ 16 = ₹2187.5.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2187.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹700

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹756

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

1. SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

2. Difference (CI − SI) for 2 years = P(R ÷ 100)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89865c95414039ebdb7e70d40e2da6d15b291165132b7b3f924e741c42f7df3a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = 700 ÷ 2 = ₹350

⇒ Since SI is same every year, 1st year interest = ₹350

⇒ CI for 1st year = SI for 1st year = ₹350

⇒ CI for 2nd year = Total CI − 1st year CI = 756 − 350 = ₹406

⇒ Difference in 2nd year interest = 406 − 350 = ₹56

⇒ This ₹56 is the interest on ₹350 for 1 year.

⇒ Rate (R) = (56 ÷ 350) × 100 = 16%

⇒ Using SI formula: 700 = (P × 16 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 700 × 100 = 32 × P

⇒ P = 70000 ÷ 32 = ₹2187.5

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2187.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference is D = P(R/100)². For 3 years, the difference is D = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Compound Interest Basics

Compound interest is essentially 'interest on interest'. For the first year (when compounded annually), SI and CI are always equal.

Rate of Interest formula from SI and CI

For a 2-year period, the rate of interest R = [2 × (CI − SI) ÷ SI] × 100%.
